White River Water Issues

By: Oelf Barnard | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
White River relies on tourism and farming for export, so when the town's water supply was cut off, it was like cutting off its blood supply.

Summary:
WHITE RIVER WATER ISSUES
The water issues in White River are huge, fueled by corruption, illegal connections and the lack of action by the Municipality of Mbombela to address these problems. The residents of this leavy town now want answers that they are not getting from the people in charge of the town's water. Piet Badenhorst, a concerned citizen of the town initiated a petition to get Carte Blanche to investigate the water issues that have plagued this town for far too long.

At a meeting that was held on the 21st of April in White River to discuss the water issues, Carol Zulu, the General Manager - Water and Sanitation of the Mbombela Municipality, as reported in the White River Post newspaper, said the main problem was the illegal tapping of power from the transformers and the clamping of valves on the pipeline that supplied water to the town. The Mhluluzi illegal informal settlement seemed to be the culprit. Zulu explained that on paper the water supply to White River was enough but due to the tapping into the power supply was a problem that could not be solved overnight. The challenge that they have is to stop the leaks of the illegal clamping of the valves.

The illegal tapping of electricity had on several occasions been taken care of and resolved but reappeared. This crime happened at night and therefore the Municipality could not prevent it and had no control over it. Zulu said that on previous occasions the residents of the settlement had become violent and protested. With bigger houses being built there, the need for more power will increase and more residents will tap electricity from the transformers resulting in worse problems.
Zulu said a new reservoir would be the answer to the problem and law-enforcement officers should be deployed to arrest the perpetrators. According to Piet Badenhorst the water issues won’t go away unless the pump stations are moved to safer premises


Further information:
WHITE RIVER WATER ISSUES – CARTE BLANCHE

1. White River, just 20 kilometres north of Mbombela, have seen a property boom with new developments after an embargo that was placed on the town had been lifted in the late nineties.

2. You may ask why an embargo was placed on the town from further development in the first place?

JOHAN WALDECK or PIET SKEAD (Chairman of Afriforum) tells us why…
(Talks about the fact that there wasn’t enough water resources back then to supply the town with water.)

3. This cosy village that lies next to the White river gets its water from two sources, from the White River irrigation scheme and the Crocodile river.

JOHAN WALDECK or PIET SKEAD explains…
(Where the water that feeds the town comes from)
Graphic to explain and shots of the dams and reservoirs.

4. The lack of rainfall normally plays a significant role in the water problems that the town normally faces, but until recently in April the town ran completely dry for two weeks and this had nothing to do with the lack of rainfall in the area.

5. We are here in White River to investigate the real story behind the water issues that have plagued this leavy town not only the past couple of months but for the past couple of years. One person that took it upon himself to start a petition to get Carte Blanche to investigate this story, is Piet Badenhorst, a business owner and concerned resident of White River.

PIET BADENHORST
Talks about his frustration when the town ran completely dry in April.

Cut to:
Case studies:

Rustig Old Age Home –

Themba Hospital

Hospice

Schools

Businesses (hair salons)

PIET BADENHORST– INTERVIEW
Explains what happened in the two weeks that they had no water and the lack of communication from the Mbombela Municipality. Intro Disaster Management.

INTERVIEW JACQUES BENADE - DISASTER MANAGEMENT
Explains what they had to do to assist in the community’s needs.

6. Piet Skead from Afriforum and a longtime resident of White River is so angry with the Mbombela Municipality, he threathens to take them to court if they don’t get their act together.

PIET SKEAD Interview
Talks about the informal settlement that jumped up on military grounds three years ago and the fact that nobody lifted a finger to stop this. Talks about the waterpipeline that travels through the informal settlement.

7. We wanted to know from Arthur Douglas from Silulumanzi what role they play in maintaining the waterpipeline to White River.

INTERVIEW ARTHUR DOUGLAS – ENGINEERING SERVICES MANAGER
Arthur Douglas from Silulmanzi explains their role in the maintenance of the pipeline and how it falls apart when it reaches the Msholozi illegal informal settlement and the Phulani Pump Station. He explains their role in maintaining this and where it all breaks down.

Cut to Informal Settlement and the transformers.

8. So, this is where White River’s water problems start! All goes well, upto here, then it all goes haywire! Suddenly you open your tap and there is no water and if you are a resident of White River, you know that you may well be without water for days and even weeks on end.

9. The transformers were here first, then came the settlement. From just a few shacks to more than ten thousand people living here now.

10. We are here to meet the person who is trying his utmost to keep the tranformers running. He asked us to hide his identity.

INTERVIEW MARTIN CONTRACTOR
Shows us what he has to deal with on a daily and hourly basis. Talks about the corruption of certain councillors that sell power and the people in the informal settlement tapping into the transformers.

INTERVIEW WITH SOME OF THE RESIDENTS OF THE SETTLEMENT
Talk about their frustrations and why they tap into the power and water supply.

11. We are on our way to the Mbombela Municipality to speak to the General Manager of Water and Sanitation, Carol Zulu. Hopefully we’ll get some answers for the residents of White River.

INTERVIEWS WITH MBOMBELA MUNICIPALITY - CAROL ZULU (GM WATER AND SANITATION)/NOKO SEANEGO (MUNICIPAL MANAGER)/OUPA MAKOENA CFO/MANDLA NKOSI (one or more of these from Mbombela Municipality will be spoken to)
Their views on the water issues issues and how they plan to rectify the illegal tapping into the power supply and the corruption that is happening under their nose. We want to know from them if they are not more concerned to keep the people of the informal settlement happy in exchange for their votes to keep the ANC ruling municipality in office.

12. The residents in the informal settlement are there to stay and we have seen that no matter how many security guards you employ or how many law enforcement officers you place there to protect the transformers, the residents’ desperation will still drive them to find ways to tap into to the power supply.

INTERVIEW WITH SOME OF THE SECURITY GUARDS/SAPS THAT PROTECT THE TRANSFORMERS
(They explain their frustrations)


13. We are meeting Piet Badenhorst and the man who knows it all, to share with us what they think the solutions to White River’s water problems are.


INTERVIEW PIET BADENHORST AND MARTIN
We ask them to explain their suggestions.

INTERVIEW CAROL ZULU
We hear her view on the suggestion that they move the transformers to another place such as the Rocky’s Drift area that Piet and Martin suggest and what her office plans to do to stop the corruption and address the water issues.

14. It is clear that the water issues are here to stay unless the Mbombela Municipality listens and addresses the corruption and the needs not only of the residents of White River but of the Msholozi Informal Settlement as well.

Press Release:


White River Water
White River relies on tourism and farming for export to survive. Every drop of water is crucial to businesses and industry in this small Mpumalanga town. But with an informal community mushrooming around critical infrastructure, and illegal electrical connections crippling water supply to the town, the White River municipality is forced to implement a controversial solution to keep the taps flowing. Carte Blanche reports.


Script:


COMMENTARY 1

White River in Mpumalanga lies between Mbombela and Hazyview on the doorstep of the popular Kruger National Park.
LINK 1
White River’s economy is based on tourism and farming for export, so when their water supply
was cut off on the 10th of April this year, it was like cutting off their blood supply…

COMMENTARY 2

The highlying areas of the town and the CBD were severely affected by water disruptions, particularly those who needed water to run their businesses.
Friendz Hairsalon – Alice Parko
It did affect my business a lot. They did not tell us that the water was going to be closed, we had to go out and look for water.
How did it affect your business?
You know our work I pay a rental of R15000 and there is no water having 20 workers and there’s no water, you know it is very difficult.

Trudie Grove-Morgan - Ward Councillor White River
The longest we have had been without water was 17 days.

COMMENTARY 3
Trudie Grove-Morgan, Ward Councillor for White River says guesthouses and lodges in town had to turn people away.

Trudie
Tourism dropped because the buses drove right through town, they didn’t stop.

Jennifer Erskine – Guesthouse Owner
We obviously have quite a number of guests coming in whether they are overnight reps or whether they are guests going to the Kruger Park, we need to be able to provide them with a constant water supply and with the interruptions that we are experiencing we have to make sure that we have an alternative source and rely on our boreholes and we have to be quite conservative.

COMMENTARY 4
The Millennium Home of Hope who takes care of special needs babies and toddlers depended on the kindness of their neighbours who shared water from their boreholes.

COMMENTARY 5
Farming operations and events planned during this time turned into a logistical nightmare.
Nottinghill Equestrian Estate – Kraai Kamffer du Preez
We had a huge problem with water because of the emptiness of the dams. It affects my property because I have horses to feed and because we have horseshows here. Specifically on the one weekend we had a huge horseshow here from the Friday to the Monday and we had no water that was coming down the canal. We have 70 horses to give water and a horse drinks about 50 litres of water per day.

COMMENTARY 6
White River gets its water from the White River Water Treatment Works, which is fed by the Longmere and Klipkopje dams. The system is also supplemented by water that comes from the Crocodile River through Mbombela and passes through the Msholozi informal settlement. All the treated water is then pumped to the White River reservoir complex and distributed to the town but the water problem has also been aggravated by the recent drought.


Dian Pretorius – White River Farmer
Due to the low rainfall and the drought that we are going through we are already on 60 percent water restrictions. The little water that we do have left we try and safe it, what makes it more complicated is all the illegal connections on the pipes and a lot of them are leaking and we are wasting quite a lot of water.

COMMENTARY 7
On the 21st of April, Trudy and the Ratepayers Association called a meeting with the Mbombela Municipality to explain to the residents of White River how they are going to solve the water crisis.

Trudie
I was tired of telling the community stories. I wanted the community to hear it from the horse’s mouth.

COMMENTARY 8
Joseph Ngala – Spokesperson for the Mbombela Municipality acknowledged that they have a serious problem with the transformer located in the Msholozi informal settlement.

Joseph Ngala
The pump station was there before the informal settlement. We have a problem here people have connected illegally that has now made the pumps tripping because of the overload on the transformer.


Trudie
There is an illegal settlement that has come up there with the years, its called Msholozi. They have been connecting directly to the transformer. The more the area grows the more the demand is for electricity.


LINK 2
But what does electricity have to do with water supply? It’s simple; electricity is needed for the pumps to pump water to homes.

Rowan Torr – Committee Member of the Ratepayers Association White River
You know White River is a very old town, it’s over a hundred years old and over the years it has grown and grown. There hasn’t been adequate water and electricity to the town for many years. So, we found ourselves now in a position, we have this big informal settlement, It is right in the path of the water that is pumped from the Crocodile River in Nelspruit through to White River.

LINK 3
It’s complicated on the one hand you have got an informal settlement, people who live there need electricity and water just to survive and on the other hand you have a thriving business community and they can’t afford to not have electricity and water for a single day.

COMMENTARY 9
Collen Mokoena who lives in the Msholozi gets his electricity from the problematic transformer at the pump station.
Collen Mokoena – Msholozi Resident
It’s not a legal connection in the meantime while they still prepare to provide electricity we are going to be using electricity from the filtration plant – the power that is coming from the filtration plant.

Joseph Ngala
They moved into an area that doesn’t even belong to the municipality, privately owned land where part of the land belongs to a local farm, the part of the land belongs to the National Department of Public Works. By law we can’t put infrastructure on land that doesn’t belong to us.


Rowan Torr
When one drives through Msholozi, one can see investment of houses going up on land, which doesn’t belong to those people. It hasn’t been proclaimed yet.

COMMENTARY 9
Victor Nake is building his dream house in the Msholozi informal settlement.
Victor Nake
Ja I built this house it cost me a lot of money and I am still not finished yet. I am still raising some money to do the finish ups.

Joseph Ngala
You can’t drive them away because once they have been in that space for a particular time, you have got to provide alternative. The Municipality has since engaged with the National Department of Public Works to say please let’s have the land transferred so that we deal also with the challenges.

COMMENTARY 10
A week after the Ratepayers meeting, Trudie went back to Msholozi to see if the municipality had kept their promises to secure the transformer.
Trudie
I went there I have seen the casing looked good but council itself did an illegal connection from the main transformer.

Joseph Ngala
We have taken a decision as the municipality that we are going to connect about 500 households because that will then address the problem of them connecting illegally on the pump station and at the same time we are trying to protect our infrastructure as well.

Trudie
We must not build a attitude of doing things illegal.

Joseph Ngala
You running the risk of them vandalising your infrastructure.
Devi
Burning it down...
Joseph Ngala
Burning it down and that has got adverse consequences.

Devi to Trudie
Do you have sympathy for the municipality?
Trudie
No I don’t have sympathy. I really don’t have sympathy for them because 98 percent of rates are paid in White River. So there is no problem that White River people do not pay. White River people need the services that they are paying for.
Devi
Is the situation going to get better or worse?
Trudie
I have a feeling that this problem will get worse if this thing is not resolved.
END.

PROMO LINK 15 SEC
White River relies on tourism and faming for export, so when the town’s water supply was cut off, it was like cutting off its blood supply.
Trudie
98 % of their rates are paid in White River. White River needs the services that they are paying for!

PROMO LINK 15 SEC
Faced with providing water and electricity to two adjacent but very different communities, the Mbombela municipality implements a drastic and controversial solution.
Joseph Ngala
You are running the risk of them vandalizing your infrastructure.
Devi
Burning it down!

PROMO LINK 10 SEC
An informal community mushrooms around critical infrastructure leaving the Mbombela municipality with no choice but to implement a controversial solution to keep the taps flowing.

Every drop of water is crucial to businesses and industry in this small Mpumalanga town. But with an informal community mushrooming around critical infrastructure, and illegal electrical connections crippling water supply to the town, the White River municipality is forced to implement a controversial solution to keep the taps flowing. Carte Blanche reports. Script: COMMENTARY 1 White River in Mpumalanga lies between Mbombela and Hazyview on the doorstep of the popular Kruger National Park. LINK 1 White River’s economy is based on tourism and farming for export, so when their water supply was cut off on the 10th of April this year, it was like cutting off their blood supply… COMMENTARY 2 The highlying areas of the town and the CBD were severely affected by water disruptions, particularly those who needed water to run their businesses. Friendz Hairsalon – Alice Parko It did affect my business a lot. They did not tell us that the water was going to be closed, we had to go out and look for water. How did it affect your business? You know our work I pay a rental of R15000 and there is no water having 20 workers and there’s no water, you know it is very difficult. Trudie Grove-Morgan - Ward Councillor White River The longest we have had been without water was 17 days. COMMENTARY 3 Trudie Grove-Morgan, Ward Councillor for White River says guesthouses and lodges in town had to turn people away. Trudie Tourism dropped because the buses drove right through town, they didn’t stop. Jennifer Erskine – Guesthouse Owner We obviously have quite a number of guests coming in whether they are overnight reps or whether they are guests going to the Kruger Park, we need to be able to provide them with a constant water supply and with the interruptions that we are experiencing we have to make sure that we have an alternative source and rely on our boreholes and we have to be quite conservative. COMMENTARY 4 The Millennium Home of Hope who takes care of special needs babies and toddlers depended on the kindness of their neighbours who shared water from their boreholes. COMMENTARY 5 Farming operations and events planned during this time turned into a logistical nightmare. Nottinghill Equestrian Estate – Kraai Kamffer du Preez We had a huge problem with water because of the emptiness of the dams. It affects my property because I have horses to feed and because we have horseshows here. Specifically on the one weekend we had a huge horseshow here from the Friday to the Monday and we had no water that was coming down the canal. We have 70 horses to give water and a horse drinks about 50 litres of water per day. COMMENTARY 6 White River gets its water from the White River Water Treatment Works, which is fed by the Longmere and Klipkopje dams. The system is also supplemented by water that comes from the Crocodile River through Mbombela and passes through the Msholozi informal settlement. All the treated water is then pumped to the White River reservoir complex and distributed to the town but the water problem has also been aggravated by the recent drought. Dian Pretorius – White River Farmer Due to the low rainfall and the drought that we are going through we are already on 60 percent water restrictions. The little water that we do have left we try and safe it, what makes it more complicated is all the illegal connections on the pipes and a lot of them are leaking and we are wasting quite a lot of water. COMMENTARY 7 On the 21st of April, Trudy and the Ratepayers Association called a meeting with the Mbombela Municipality to explain to the residents of White River how they are going to solve the water crisis. Trudie I was tired of telling the community stories. I wanted the community to hear it from the horse’s mouth. COMMENTARY 8 Joseph Ngala – Spokesperson for the Mbombela Municipality acknowledged that they have a serious problem with the transformer located in the Msholozi informal settlement. Joseph Ngala The pump station was there before the informal settlement. We have a problem here people have connected illegally that has now made the pumps tripping because of the overload on the transformer. Trudie There is an illegal settlement that has come up there with the years, its called Msholozi. They have been connecting directly to the transformer. The more the area grows the more the demand is for electricity. LINK 2 But what does electricity have to do with water supply? It’s simple; electricity is needed for the pumps to pump water to homes. Rowan Torr – Committee Member of the Ratepayers Association White River You know White River is a very old town, it’s over a hundred years old and over the years it has grown and grown. There hasn’t been adequate water and electricity to the town for many years. So, we found ourselves now in a position, we have this big informal settlement, It is right in the path of the water that is pumped from the Crocodile River in Nelspruit through to White River. LINK 3 It’s complicated on the one hand you have got an informal settlement, people who live there need electricity and water just to survive and on the other hand you have a thriving business community and they can’t afford to not have electricity and water for a single day. COMMENTARY 9 Collen Mokoena who lives in the Msholozi gets his electricity from the problematic transformer at the pump station. Collen Mokoena – Msholozi Resident It’s not a legal connection in the meantime while they still prepare to provide electricity we are going to be using electricity from the filtration plant – the power that is coming from the filtration plant. Joseph Ngala They moved into an area that doesn’t even belong to the municipality, privately owned land where part of the land belongs to a local farm, the part of the land belongs to the National Department of Public Works. By law we can’t put infrastructure on land that doesn’t belong to us. Rowan Torr When one drives through Msholozi, one can see investment of houses going up on land, which doesn’t belong to those people. It hasn’t been proclaimed yet. COMMENTARY 9 Victor Nake is building his dream house in the Msholozi informal settlement. Victor Nake Ja I built this house it cost me a lot of money and I am still not finished yet. I am still raising some money to do the finish ups. Joseph Ngala You can’t drive them away because once they have been in that space for a particular time, you have got to provide alternative. The Municipality has since engaged with the National Department of Public Works to say please let’s have the land transferred so that we deal also with the challenges. COMMENTARY 10 A week after the Ratepayers meeting, Trudie went back to Msholozi to see if the municipality had kept their promises to secure the transformer. Trudie I went there I have seen the casing looked good but council itself did an illegal connection from the main transformer. Joseph Ngala We have taken a decision as the municipality that we are going to connect about 500 households because that will then address the problem of them connecting illegally on the pump station and at the same time we are trying to protect our infrastructure as well. Trudie We must not build a attitude of doing things illegal. Joseph Ngala You running the risk of them vandalising your infrastructure. Devi Burning it down... Joseph Ngala Burning it down and that has got adverse consequences. Devi to Trudie Do you have sympathy for the municipality? Trudie No I don’t have sympathy. I really don’t have sympathy for them because 98 percent of rates are paid in White River. So there is no problem that White River people do not pay. White River people need the services that they are paying for. Devi Is the situation going to get better or worse? Trudie I have a feeling that this problem will get worse if this thing is not resolved. END. PROMO LINK 15 SEC White River relies on tourism and faming for export, so when the town’s water supply was cut off, it was like cutting off its blood supply. Trudie 98 % of their rates are paid in White River. White River needs the services that they are paying for! PROMO LINK 15 SEC Faced with providing water and electricity to two adjacent but very different communities, the Mbombela municipality implements a drastic and controversial solution. Joseph Ngala You are running the risk of them vandalizing your infrastructure. Devi Burning it down! PROMO LINK 10 SEC An informal community mushrooms around critical infrastructure leaving the Mbombela municipality with no choice but to implement a controversial solution to keep the taps flowing. metadata.Summary: WHITE RIVER WATER ISSUES The water issues in White River are huge, fueled by corruption, illegal connections and the lack of action by the Municipality of Mbombela to address these problems. The residents of this leavy town now want answers that they are not getting from the people in charge of the town's water. Piet Badenhorst, a concerned citizen of the town initiated a petition to get Carte Blanche to investigate the water issues that have plagued this town for far too long. At a meeting that was held on the 21st of April in White River to discuss the water issues, Carol Zulu, the General Manager - Water and Sanitation of the Mbombela Municipality, as reported in the White River Post newspaper, said the main problem was the illegal tapping of power from the transformers and the clamping of valves on the pipeline that supplied water to the town. The Mhluluzi illegal informal settlement seemed to be the culprit. Zulu explained that on paper the water supply to White River was enough but due to the tapping into the power supply was a problem that could not be solved overnight. The challenge that they have is to stop the leaks of the illegal clamping of the valves. The illegal tapping of electricity had on several occasions been taken care of and resolved but reappeared. This crime happened at night and therefore the Municipality could not prevent it and had no control over it. Zulu said that on previous occasions the residents of the settlement had become violent and protested. With bigger houses being built there, the need for more power will increase and more residents will tap electricity from the transformers resulting in worse problems. Zulu said a new reservoir would be the answer to the problem and law-enforcement officers should be deployed to arrest the perpetrators. According to Piet Badenhorst the water issues won’t go away unless the pump stations are moved to safer premises
metadata.Further information: WHITE RIVER WATER ISSUES – CARTE BLANCHE 1. White River, just 20 kilometres north of Mbombela, have seen a property boom with new developments after an embargo that was placed on the town had been lifted in the late nineties. 2. You may ask why an embargo was placed on the town from further development in the first place? JOHAN WALDECK or PIET SKEAD (Chairman of Afriforum) tells us why… (Talks about the fact that there wasn’t enough water resources back then to supply the town with water.) 3. This cosy village that lies next to the White river gets its water from two sources, from the White River irrigation scheme and the Crocodile river. JOHAN WALDECK or PIET SKEAD explains… (Where the water that feeds the town comes from) Graphic to explain and shots of the dams and reservoirs. 4. The lack of rainfall normally plays a significant role in the water problems that the town normally faces, but until recently in April the town ran completely dry for two weeks and this had nothing to do with the lack of rainfall in the area. 5. We are here in White River to investigate the real story behind the water issues that have plagued this leavy town not only the past couple of months but for the past couple of years. One person that took it upon himself to start a petition to get Carte Blanche to investigate this story, is Piet Badenhorst, a business owner and concerned resident of White River. PIET BADENHORST Talks about his frustration when the town ran completely dry in April. Cut to: Case studies: Rustig Old Age Home – Themba Hospital Hospice Schools Businesses (hair salons) PIET BADENHORST– INTERVIEW Explains what happened in the two weeks that they had no water and the lack of communication from the Mbombela Municipality. Intro Disaster Management. INTERVIEW JACQUES BENADE - DISASTER MANAGEMENT Explains what they had to do to assist in the community’s needs. 6. Piet Skead from Afriforum and a longtime resident of White River is so angry with the Mbombela Municipality, he threathens to take them to court if they don’t get their act together. PIET SKEAD Interview Talks about the informal settlement that jumped up on military grounds three years ago and the fact that nobody lifted a finger to stop this. Talks about the waterpipeline that travels through the informal settlement. 7. We wanted to know from Arthur Douglas from Silulumanzi what role they play in maintaining the waterpipeline to White River. INTERVIEW ARTHUR DOUGLAS – ENGINEERING SERVICES MANAGER Arthur Douglas from Silulmanzi explains their role in the maintenance of the pipeline and how it falls apart when it reaches the Msholozi illegal informal settlement and the Phulani Pump Station. He explains their role in maintaining this and where it all breaks down. Cut to Informal Settlement and the transformers. 8. So, this is where White River’s water problems start! All goes well, upto here, then it all goes haywire! Suddenly you open your tap and there is no water and if you are a resident of White River, you know that you may well be without water for days and even weeks on end. 9. The transformers were here first, then came the settlement. From just a few shacks to more than ten thousand people living here now. 10. We are here to meet the person who is trying his utmost to keep the tranformers running. He asked us to hide his identity. INTERVIEW MARTIN CONTRACTOR Shows us what he has to deal with on a daily and hourly basis. Talks about the corruption of certain councillors that sell power and the people in the informal settlement tapping into the transformers. INTERVIEW WITH SOME OF THE RESIDENTS OF THE SETTLEMENT Talk about their frustrations and why they tap into the power and water supply. 11. We are on our way to the Mbombela Municipality to speak to the General Manager of Water and Sanitation, Carol Zulu. Hopefully we’ll get some answers for the residents of White River. INTERVIEWS WITH MBOMBELA MUNICIPALITY - CAROL ZULU (GM WATER AND SANITATION)/NOKO SEANEGO (MUNICIPAL MANAGER)/OUPA MAKOENA CFO/MANDLA NKOSI (one or more of these from Mbombela Municipality will be spoken to) Their views on the water issues issues and how they plan to rectify the illegal tapping into the power supply and the corruption that is happening under their nose. We want to know from them if they are not more concerned to keep the people of the informal settlement happy in exchange for their votes to keep the ANC ruling municipality in office. 12. The residents in the informal settlement are there to stay and we have seen that no matter how many security guards you employ or how many law enforcement officers you place there to protect the transformers, the residents’ desperation will still drive them to find ways to tap into to the power supply. INTERVIEW WITH SOME OF THE SECURITY GUARDS/SAPS THAT PROTECT THE TRANSFORMERS (They explain their frustrations) 13. We are meeting Piet Badenhorst and the man who knows it all, to share with us what they think the solutions to White River’s water problems are. INTERVIEW PIET BADENHORST AND MARTIN We ask them to explain their suggestions. INTERVIEW CAROL ZULU We hear her view on the suggestion that they move the transformers to another place such as the Rocky’s Drift area that Piet and Martin suggest and what her office plans to do to stop the corruption and address the water issues. 14. It is clear that the water issues are here to stay unless the Mbombela Municipality listens and addresses the corruption and the needs not only of the residents of White River but of the Msholozi Informal Settlement as well.
